title: Money

parent.learn: Know the Indian coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20) and notes (₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100).
parent.why: The number printed on the coin or note is what it is worth — not its size. A bigger coin is not always worth more.

parent.learn: Add coins to make an amount.
parent.why: ₹5 and ₹2 is ₹7: adding money is the same adding as with apples, just with a ₹ sign.

parent.learn: The same amount can be made in different ways.
parent.why: ₹10 can be one ₹10 coin, two ₹5 coins, or five ₹2 coins. This is what “change” at the shop is about.

parent.learn: Change is what you get back.
parent.why: If something costs ₹6 and you pay ₹10, the shopkeeper gives back ₹10 − ₹6 = ₹4. Change is taking away.

ask: Look at a ₹5 coin: what number is on it?
Play shop at home: a toffee costs ₹2. Pay me.
You have ₹5. Can you buy a ₹10 toy?
A banana is ₹3 and an apple is ₹4. How much for both?
I pay ₹10 for a ₹7 pen. What change do I get?

rounds.h: 10 is the biggest number, so the ₹10 coin is worth the most.
We pay money at the shop to buy what we need.

rounds.t: A ₹5 coin and a ₹1 coin make…
A toffee costs ₹2. You have ₹5. Can you buy it?
rounds.h: ₹5 is more than ₹2, so you have enough — and some left over.

rounds.t: A ball costs ₹10. You have ₹5. How much more do you need?
Which note is the biggest amount?
A pencil costs ₹5 and an eraser costs ₹3. How much for both?
A chocolate costs ₹6. You pay ₹10. How much change do you get back?
rounds.h: Change = what you paid − the price: 10 − 6 = 4.
Count in twos up to 10: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 — that is 5 coins.

rounds.t: One ₹20 note is the same as how many ₹10 notes?
